clue.text: Rate: catch for case

parts.note: to rate someone is to scold them, as is to carpet them
to bag game is to catch it

explanation.surface: A terse note pairing a price rate with a catch, as if from a ledger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rate' here is the old verb meaning to tell off, not a price; CARPET means the same, as in being 'called on the carpet'.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpetbag is a travelling bag, i.e. a kind of luggage case.

clue.text: Chap under canvas drops mass in skip

indicators.note: drops means the letter for mass falls out of the word

parts.note: a man sleeping in a tent is a camper
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A man in a tent loses some weight while skipping about.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to leap or skip about playfully.

clue.text: List includes old bird

indicators.note: includes means the duty list takes a letter inside it

parts.note: a roster is a list of names on duty

explanation.surface: A register of names contains an aged bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a male domestic fowl, a cockerel.

clue.text: River crustacean the French find very bad

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England
a crab is a crustacean
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A crab from a river, served the French way, turns out to be awful.
explanation.definitionFit: Execrable means utterly dreadful, deserving to be cursed.

clue.text: Find oneself at pill cabinet, looking for this?

definitions.text: Find oneself at pill cabinet, looking for this?

parts.note: to find oneself at a place is simply to be there
a tab is a tablet or pill
a locker is a small lockable cabinet

explanation.surface: Someone stands at the medicine cabinet, hunting for a particular drug.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and a picture of a patient seeking the drug at the medicine cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A beta blocker is a heart drug taken as pills, the very thing one might seek in a medicine cabinet.

clue.text: Breathe with difficulty, with lack of pressure in air

indicators.note: with lack of means the letter for pressure goes missing

parts.note: to gasp is to breathe with difficulty
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Someone gasps for breath at altitude where the air pressure is low.
explanation.definitionFit: Air is a gas, the mixture of gases we breathe.

clue.text: Penny leaves university life for a writer

indicators.note: leaves means the letter for penny departs from the word

parts.note: campus life is life at university, so campus stands for it

explanation.surface: A student named Penny drops out of college to become an author.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Camus was the French writer of The Outsider.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Camus was a French novelist and essayist, an example of a writer.

clue.text: Conservative socks preferred

parts.note: hose means stockings or socks

explanation.surface: A traditionalist picks the socks he likes best.
explanation.definitionFit: Chose is the past tense of choose, meaning picked or preferred.

clue.text: Dean's one, for a tipple

parts.note: Dean Martin, the American singer, supplies his surname
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A college dean has his own favourite drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dean' looks like a college official, but it is the first name of the crooner Dean Martin.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin and vermouth, a kind of drink.

clue.text: Jocular way. to address a relative of Winchester?

definitions.meaning: a jokey, affectionate form of address to a man
the Winchester rifle is a gun, so its offspring would be a gun's child

explanation.surface: A friendly greeting fit for kin of a famous rifle.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a jocular address to a man, and read literally names the offspring of a firearm such as a Winchester.

clue.text: Object for an international match

parts.note: pro is Latin for 'for', meaning in favour of
a Test is an international cricket or rugby match

explanation.surface: Someone raises an objection about a big international fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: To object is to protest, both verbs of expressing disapproval.

clue.text: Kinky porn star hasn't time for leather pouch

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent into a new order
hasn't means the letter for time is missing from the fodder

explanation.surface: A risque film performer is described as lacking time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't' removes T from PORNSTAR, leaving PORNSAR, which 'Kinky' rearranges. A sporran is the pouch worn at the front of a Scottish kilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporran is the leather pouch hung in front of a Highland kilt.

clue.text: It turns left and right

indicators.note: left and right says the word reads the same from either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something that swings to the left and to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole word is the wordplay: it reads identically from left to right and from right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine, so it is the thing that turns.

clue.text: Moore may have produced this graduate's financial assistance

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate, with the possessive giving S
relief is aid given to those in need

explanation.surface: A graduate receives a grant to study the work of Moore.
explanation.walkthrough: Moore is Henry Moore, the English sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Bas-relief is low-relief sculpture, the kind of work a sculptor like Henry Moore might make.

clue.text: Times to be taken off the shelf?

definitions.text: Times to be taken off the shelf?

parts.words: Times to be taken off the shelf?
parts.note: the moments printed on food packets after which shops must remove the goods from sale

explanation.surface: Questions about when stock should be cleared from shop shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the dates on packaging by which a shop must sell or withdraw perishable goods.

clue.text: Flyers going back a long way

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, are flyers

explanation.surface: Airmen returning from a long distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Far means at a great distance, a long way off.

clue.text: Relatives of a vampire preferring blood oranges?

definitions.text: Relatives of a vampire preferring blood oranges?

parts.words: Relatives of a vampire preferring blood oranges?
parts.note: kin of the blood-sucking vampire bat whose diet is fruit rather than blood

explanation.surface: A vampire's family that prefers fruit to blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit bats are bats that feed on fruit, relatives of the vampire bat.

clue.text: Asking for-money to secure criminal tool is illicit activity

indicators.note: to secure means the begging holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: begging is asking for money

indicators.note: criminal means wrong or bent, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A beggar raises funds to buy a crook's implement, which is illegal.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'for-money' is a print quirk; 'criminal' looks like it describes the tool but signals the anagram, and 'to secure' wraps the begging round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootlegging is illegally making or selling liquor or goods, an illicit trade.

clue.text: Throw grenade at hound

indicators.note: throw means the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier hurls a grenade at a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A Great Dane is a very large breed of dog, a hound.

clue.text: The hardest tongue twisters are dreadful

definitions.meaning: taken literally, the toughest twisters cannot be said at all
awful, too bad to be described

explanation.surface: The trickiest tongue twisters are terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means too bad for words, and literally names what cannot be spoken, like the hardest tongue twisters.

clue.text: Gratuitous offering in transport allowance

indicators.note: in means the gratuity sits inside the other word

parts.note: to send someone is to transport them, as with delight
a tip is a gratuity, an extra offering

explanation.surface: A tip is slipped into the travel expenses.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular allowance or salary.

clue.text: Announcing happy event in paper?

indicators.note: announcing means the word is spoken, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: the birth of a son is a happy event

explanation.surface: A birth announcement placed in a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun is a British daily newspaper, so a paper.

clue.text: Get hold of a bit

definitions.meaning: a horse's bit with a jointed mouthpiece

explanation.surface: Grab hold of a small piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To snaffle is to take or seize, and a snaffle is a simple jointed bit for a horse.

clue.text: Scaffolder laying into delinquent gets fired

indicators.note: laying into means the scaffolder is placed inside the delinquent

parts.note: a Ted, short for Teddy boy, is a 1950s British youth delinquent
a rigger puts up scaffolding

explanation.surface: A builder attacks a young thug and gets sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teddy boy was a 1950s British youth known for Edwardian dress and rowdiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Triggered means set off, as a gun is fired by its trigger.

clue.text: Complaint raised, say, about rough water

indicators.note: about means the reversed letters go round the other piece
raised means read upwards in this down clue, so reversed

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
a rip is a stretch of turbulent water

explanation.surface: A grumble is raised about choppy seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns EG into GE, which goes 'about' RIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A gripe is a grumble or complaint.

clue.text: Market turned penny for vagrant

indicators.note: turned means the word is reversed

parts.note: a mart is a market

explanation.surface: A trader gives back a penny to a homeless person.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a homeless wanderer, a vagrant.

clue.text: From pair, keeping one horse

indicators.note: keeping means the pair holds the other letters inside

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: Out of a pair, one horse is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacer is a horse trained to pace, as in harness racing.

clue.text: Pleasurable aspect of type of hospital bed.

definitions.meaning: a pleasant feature, as of a place
in British hospitals, a private bed a patient pays extra for

explanation.surface: A ward's private bed is among its nicer features.
explanation.definitionFit: An amenity is a pleasant feature, and an amenity bed is a paid private bed in an NHS hospital.

clue.text: Unknown before noon to eat 'this?

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown
am stands for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: A question about what to eat in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A yam is an edible tuber, something to eat.

clue.text: Truck will be part of it

definitions.text: Truck will be part of it

parts.words: Truck will be part of it
parts.note: a lorry on the road belongs to the flow of vehicles, and truck also means dealings

explanation.surface: A lorry joining the flow of vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic is vehicles on the road, which include trucks, and also trade, which is what truck means.

clue.text: Notice closing extremely disappointing plant

indicators.note: closing means the word for notice shuts around the other letters

parts.note: to see is to notice

indicators.note: extremely picks the outermost letters of the word

explanation.surface: A notice of closure that is thoroughly disappointing for gardeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives DG, the first and last letters of 'disappointing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grasslike plant growing in wet ground.

clue.text: Converted Turk: see me in Athos 'perhaps

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Turk who has changed faith invites someone to visit.
explanation.walkthrough: Athos is one of Dumas's Three Musketeers.
explanation.definitionFit: Athos is one of the three musketeers in Dumas's novel, an example of the type.
